'''''Acis autumnalis''''', the '''autumn snowflake''',<ref name=GreyMathBlam81/> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Amaryllidaceae]]. A short [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]], it is found on the western shores of the Mediterranean, from Portugal, Spain and Morocco to Sicily and Tunisia.

==Description==
''Acis autumnalis'' grows to about {{cvt|10|–|15|cm|in|0}} tall. Its leaves are narrow, often seeming to form tufts, and usually only appear after the flowers. ''A. autumnalis'' flowers in late summer to autumn, with one to four flowers per stalk, each carried on a long, thin [[pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]. The white [[tepal]]s are 9–14 mm long, pinkish at the base, less commonly all pink. The outer three tepals are toothed. There is normally only one [[spathe]] at the base of the flowers.<ref name=GreyMathBlam81/><ref name=Math87/>

==Taxonomy==
''Acis autumnalis'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753, as ''Leucojum autumnale''.<ref name=IPNI_Leucojum_autumnale/> [[Richard Anthony Salisbury]] in 1807 in ''[[The Paradisus Londinensis]]'' was the first to suggest putting ''Leucojum autumnale'' in a new genus, ''Acis'',<ref name=Sali05/> although he did not actually use the name ''Acis autumnale'', which was first published in 1829 by [[Robert Sweet (botanist)|Robert Sweet]].<ref name=IPNI_Acis_autumnalis/> Most later botanists did not accept the distinction between ''Leucojum'' and ''Acis''.<ref name=Math87/><ref name=Lled04/> The genus, and with it ''Acis autumnalis'', was reinstated in 2004, after it was determined on morphological and molecular grounds that, when broadly defined, ''Leucojum'' is [[Paraphyly|paraphyletic]].<ref name=Lled04/>

The species has been divided into a number of varieties, differing in minor characters. For example, ''A. autumnalis'' var. ''diphyllum'' from North Africa has two spathes.<ref name=Math87/> The [[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] regards all the varieties as part of a single species.<ref name=WCSP_293461/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Acis autumnalis'' is found on both sides of the western [[Mediterranean]]. In Europe, it is native to Portugal, Spain (including the [[Balearic Islands]]), [[Sardinia]] and [[Sicily]]. In north Africa, it is native to [[Morocco]], [[Algeria]] and [[Tunisia]].<ref name=WCSP_293461/> It occurs in rocky places and stony hillsides.<ref name=GreyMathBlam81/><ref name=Math87/>

==Cultivation==
''Acis autumnalis'' is grown as an [[ornamental plant]]. It is recommended for light soils in sheltered positions in full sun. Some forms in cultivation increase rapidly from seeds, others from bulb division.<ref name=Math87/> The species has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=RHS/>
